title: Teacher-made example adverts (text only)
subject: PSHE
source: Written for pshe/y6 lesson 18 (Teacher-made example adverts (text only))
intro: Lesson 18: Stereotyping and judgement. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

blocks.h: Example adverts (made up, text only, no people pictured)

panels.title: Advert 1: SuperFix toolkit
panels.text: Every dad needs SuperFix! Mums, buy one for the man of the house. He will finally fix that shelf.

panels.title: Advert 2: SparkleClean spray
panels.text: Girls love a sparkling kitchen! Make Mum proud with SparkleClean, the spray every good daughter uses.

panels.title: Advert 3: GameZone headset
panels.text: Real gamers are teenage boys. Grandparents, don't even try: this headset is too clever for you!

blocks.answers: 1: only men do repairs. Fair: 'Anyone can fix that shelf with SuperFix.' 2: cleaning is for women and girls. Fair: 'Everyone can help keep the kitchen sparkling.' 3: only teenage boys game; older people cannot use technology. Fair: 'Gamers of every age enjoy GameZone; many grandparents play too.'

panels.title: Muslims and stereotypes
points: Muslims are sometimes stereotyped in media
So we must never stereotype others either

keywords.def: a fixed, unfair idea about a whole group
facts that show what is true

questions.q: Challenge with evidence: 'Old people can't use computers.'
questions.a: 'Many older people use computers well; my grandad video-calls every day.'

questions.q: Pupil PDF: find three stereotypes in example adverts (teacher-made, no people pictured) and rewrite each fairly.
Extend: write a class rule about fair judgement.

questions.a: A) much negative assumption. Assumptions can be sinful.

questions.q: Think again: Why do you think adverts often show the same kinds of people doing the same jobs?
questions.a: Habit and assumptions; it can spread stereotypes that limit people.
